My land is 8 mu on the flat plain south of the county seat. Good soil, reliable ground for wheat and corn. My family has worked this land for generations. I didn't go to school but I know this land. I know the seasons.

There is no question about what I grow. Everyone here grows winter wheat, then summer corn on the same fields. My mother grew wheat and corn. My neighbors grow wheat and corn. The grain station buys wheat and corn. This is what Quzhou does.

For wheat seed, I buy from the village seed shop — they sell the improved varieties the county recommends. Not my grandfather's old seeds, those don't yield enough. For corn I buy hybrid seed, 郑单958 or whatever the shop has this year. Hybrids cost more but the ears are bigger and fuller. Worth it.

Fertilizer — before I sow wheat I spread compound fertilizer into the soil, then I put down urea when the wheat starts to joint in spring. Same idea for corn. I do what my neighbor Wang does. She gets good harvests.

Water is the big worry. Wheat needs water here, the sky doesn't give enough. I pump from the well: once before winter to help it root, once at jointing, once when it heads, maybe once more if it's dry at grain fill. That's usually four times. Corn gets summer rain mostly, but if July is dry I'll pump once or twice.

I spray herbicide in the wheat in early spring — the weeds come up thick. Then I spray something at heading if I see rust or aphids. For corn I spray herbicide right after it comes up, and if the corn borer is bad like last year, I spray again.

After corn harvest in October I run the rotary tiller before sowing wheat. For corn in June I sow straight into the wheat stubble — no plowing. That's what everyone does now. Saves time and diesel.
